articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Dielectrically Separated Independent Gates Junctionless DG-MOSFET: A Digital Perspective
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFET) have been downscaled in response to the growing need for small, battery-operated semiconductor devices. However, the existence of significant short channel effect has hindered MOSFET downscaling beyond the nanometer regime. Drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL), velocity saturation, and quantum confinement are examples of these phenomena. To minimize these adverse implications, researchers developed the double gate (DG) MOSFET. Furthermore, the formation of abrupt junctions at deep technological nodes is another barrier to MOSFET downscaling. To solve this problem, junctionless (JL) MOSFETs are used, which have uniform doping in all three areas (Source, Channel, and Drain).For the circuit’s efficient performance, we will use the dielectrically separated independent gates (DSIG) double gate MOSFET. Moreover, from digital IC point of view, logic gates are the basic building blocks and device dimensions play a critical role in their performance. Beyond that, we'll study at how the device dimensions of dielectric separated independent gates (DSIG) JL-DG-MOSFETs impact the behaviour of fundamental logic gates including NOT, NAND, and NOR.

articleTitle: Impact of PECVD characteristics on metrics of a Plasma-Assisted Vertically Aligned Carbon Nanotube FET (VA-CNTFET) device
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This research aims to navigate discussion away from a Silicon based FET device by focusing on a relatively new design material - Carbon Nanotube as channel material. To do the same, a simulation analysis of the device Vertically Aligned Carbon Nanotube FET (VA-CNTFET) is done and investigated. The CNTs are vertically aligned owing to PECVD synthesis technique where a vertically aligned semiconducting CNT is incorporated as the channel. This investigation further draws a relation between the PECVD parameters and the metrics of the proposed device.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power 2-Bit Flash ADC using High Performance Dynamic Double Tail Comparator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The design and development of low power electronics has garnered a lot of interest in the recent past due to rise of Internet of Things. The majority of IoT enabled devices rely on reliable data mining and data handling techniques that process both analog and digital data. The present manuscript focusses on the design of an ultra-low power 2- bit flash analog to digital converter. The flash analog to digital converter is implemented using a modified double-tail latch type comparator that consumes a minimal power of 0.65 µW and a delay of 133ps for an operational voltage of 0.6V at 16m technological node. The proposed analog to digital converter is equipped with bubble error correction and digital encoding techniques for fast and reliable data conversion. The proposed analog to digital converter consumes a power of 0.4 mW at the lowest operational voltage of 0.6V for 16nm technological node. The simulation of the proposed flash analog to digital converter yields a sub-milliwatt power consumption at different operational voltage ranging from 0.6V to 1.2V. The low power consumption values suggest the use of proposed flash analog to digital converter in designing next generation of portable, handheld and energy efficient low power electronic devices that are compatible with IoT technologies.

articleTitle: Slot waveguide microring resonator based on silicon nitride for refractive index sensing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this paper, a Silicon Nitride Slot waveguide-based ring resonator has been designed, simulated, and analyzed using numerical methods. The proposed structure achieved a maximum Q-Factor of 551.6. The structure shows a sensitivity of 42.1nm/RIU. This can be utilized in refractive index sensing applications.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Low-Power High Performance 4-Bit Parallel Shift Register using Retentive True Single Phase Clocked D-Flip Flop
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: With increase in internet enabled smart systems, circuit miniaturization and low-operating power levels are given much priority in designing next-generation integrated circuits. Shift registers are commonly used electronic devices for data storage and transmission. The performance of a shift register depends on its internal circuitry that include type of technological node, design architecture and operating power levels. The present study focuses on the design and development of 4-bit parallel in parallel out (PIPO) shift register using retentive true single phase clocked (TSPC) D flip-flop. The manuscript initially demonstrates the performance of retentive true single phase clocked D flip-flop, that makes up the proposed 4-bit PIPO shift register using 16nm technological node yielding a minimum power consumption level 0.75μW at an operational voltage of 0.8V. The power consumption of the individual TSPC D flip-flop is analyzed by varying operating voltages from 0.7V to 1.2V and its results are presented. Lastly, the 4-bit PIPO shift register is designed using TSPC flip-flop and its operation and performance is discussed. The designed 4-bit PIPO shift register can be operated below 1V operating voltage to yield minimal power consumption of around 2μW. The proposed 4-bit PIPO shift register can be possibly implemented in low power energy-efficient data handling electronic devices, which has the true potential to match current industry needs.

Author Keywords: Parallel In Parallel Out Shift Register

articleTitle: Junctionless Tunnel FET for High-Temperature Applications from an Analog Design Perspective
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Junctionless transistor (JLT) is known for improved short channel effects (SCE) and hence better scalability, and high temperature advantages, in addition that it offers more convenient fabrication steps. A Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (TFET) offers theoretically possible limit of subthreshold swing (SS) and has applicability for low power electronics. TFETs demonstrated in junctionless mode led to the evolution of JL-TFETs. This work analyses the performance of a JL-TFET for high temperature applications and the same is compared with a conventional p-i-n Silicon-on-Insulator Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (p-i-n SOI-TFET) at same threshold voltage. Using calibrated technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulations, analog circuit performance parameters such as transconductance (G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>), gate-to-source capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS</inf>), gate-to-drain capacitance (C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf>), and cut-off frequency (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf>) are analyzed for variation in temperature. Response to temperature is represented in terms of electrical parameters such as threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>), on-off current ratio (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf>), subthreshold swing (SS). The ON-state current of the JL-TFET increases in order of hundreds of μA/μm at high temperature, whereas p-i-n SOI-TFET shows lesser temperature sensitivity.

articleTitle: A review on P3HT:PCBM material based organic solar cells
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Photovoltaic cells are used to convert solar energy which is an untapped and surplus energy resource available in nature into electricity. Inorganic material based solar cells are unaffordable as it is costly. Cheap cost and easy fabrication is one of the reasons for increased popularity of organic material based solar cells. Various researches are under progress to enhance the PCE (Power -Conversion Efficiency), stability and lifetime of organic material based solar cells. The type of active layer and its thickness is a major factor in enhancing the performance of OSC (organic solar-cells). This paper reviews P3HT:PCBM active-layer materials and its effects on the stability and performance of OSC.

articleTitle: Impact of Channel Thickness on the Performance of JL-DG MOSFET based NAND, NOR, and NOT Logic Gates
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The ever-increasing demand for portable electronic devices has led to the downscaling of metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) field effect transistors (FETs). However, the downscaling of MOSFET beyond nanometer regime have been stuck by the presence of lethal short channel effects. These effects include velocity saturation, drain induced barrier lowering (DIBL), and quantum confinements etc. To overcome these effects researchers have introduced the double-gate (DG) MOSFET. However, the formation of abrupt junction at deep technology nodes is another constraint to downscaling of MOSFETs. To get rid of this problem, junctionless (JL) MOSFET comes into picture that have all the regions (source, channel, and drain) uniformly doped. Moreover, from digital IC point of view, logic gates are the basic building blocks. Also, the performance analysis of logic gates is an essential requirement to understand the performance of JL-DG-MOSFET for digital ICs. Subsequently, this paper presents the effect of JL-DG-MOSFET on the performance of fundamental logic gates like NOT, NAND, and NOR gate.

articleTitle: Tunable Plasmon Resonance in Asymmetric Plasmonic Cross-Bowtie Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: An asymmetric crossed plasmonic nanobowtie nanostructure on a glass (SiO2) substrate is presented and numerically examined. The plasmon resonance and the electric-field enhancement obtained at the center of the crossed asymmetric bowties is modelled with the help of Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) simulator. The effect of the degree of asymmetricity in the flare angle of the bowties, the length of the bowties and the gap between the bowties on the nature of reflectance spectra is numerically computed and discussed. The proposed asymmetric plasmonic cross-bowtie nanostructures could be of significant importance for applications in biosensing, solid-state lighting, and fluorescence microscopy.

articleTitle: RTL to GDSII Flow Implementation of 8-bit Baugh-Wooley Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this paper, the implementation of the Baugh-Wooley multiplier for 8-bit signed multiplication is performed from RTL to GDSII generation to incorporate the physical design (PD) flow. Firstly, the RTL file is generated using the Verilog implementation of an 8-bit signed Baugh-Wooley multiplier and this RTL file is used while going through PD flow. For RTL to GDSII flow the open-source EDA tools are used for different intermediate levels such as synthesis, placement, routing, and timing analysis. Profuse results like power, area, timing constraints, layout, and frequency are incorporated and compared between the two technology nodes: 180 nm and 45 nm. In addition to this, the results of Baugh-Wooley multiplier are quantified with Booth Multiplier. By incorporating both the multipliers, it is seen that the Baugh-Wooley multiplier requires 36.68 % less area than the Booth multiplier and hence it is area efficient. However, it requires 44.60 % more power and 60 % more delay. The Baugh-Wooley multiplier is preferred if area is concerned with better slack, while Booth Multiplier can be preferred if power is concerned. In this paper, the proposed Baugh-Wooley multiplier delay and power constraints are also compared with other works.

articleTitle: Parameterized Comparison of Carbon Nanotube and Graphene Nanoribbon Field Effective Transistor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this paper, performance analysis of carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNTFET) and graphene nano-ribbon field-effect transistors (GNRFET) is done based on transfer characteristics, cut-off frequency, total charge, intrinsic delay, and transconductance by varying parameters such as temperature, oxide thickness, and channel length. After thorough investigation, it was inferred that gate-all- around CNTFET (GAA-CNTFET) and double-gate GNRFET (DG-GNRFET) had a better performance compared to back-gate CNTFET (BG-CNTFET) and back-gate GNRFET (BG-GNRFET). It’s observed that for higher values of voltages, GAA-CNTFET has almost 16.67% higher drain current than DG-GNRFET. The transconductance of GAA-CNTFET also outperforms DG-GNRFET for higher values of voltages. DG- GNRFETs have performed better compared to GAA- CNTFETs when it comes to cut-off frequency. At voltage around 1 V, when the temperature is kept constant, GAA-CNTFET shows 19.36 times more cut-off frequency than DG-GNRFET. Time delay of GAA- CNTFET is 33% more than DG-GNRFET when oxide thickness is 2nm.

articleTitle: Performance Evolution of GaAs-Based Solar Cell Towards >30% Efficiency for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This work investigates the performance of GaAs-based solar cells towards 30% efficiency for space applications. GaAs has a bandgap of 1.42 eV and it is lightweight and flexible. GaAs can absorb higher number of photons and thus exhibit high efficiency. This work has been performed using SCAPS-1D software with the main focus on optimizing the absorber layer thickness in terms of solar cell performance metrics such as fill-factor (FF), efficiency (η), J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>, and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>. The highest efficiency of 30.16% has been obtained for the optimized value of the absorber layer thickness of 200 µm, with values of 1.0275 V, 33.168453 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and 88.49% for V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>, and Fill Factor respectively. Thus, GaAs-based solar cell paves the way for space applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing the properties of Carbon fiber thermoplastic composite by nanofiber interleaving
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Thermoplastic composites have growing significance due to the rising demand for cost-effective and lightweight materials with high structural endurance and recyclability. The composition of composites is altered to enhance their overall properties. Electrospun Polyacrylonitrile nanofiber interleaving in Carbon fiber thermoplastic composite is investigated in this paper. Material properties are estimated using Tensile, Izod, Charpy, and Ballistic testing. Experimental results suggest that the nanofiber interleaving resulted in a composite with enhanced properties. The study can be further extended in investigating the effect of nanofibrous addition in various composites.

articleTitle: RF Performance Assessment of Sub-8nm GaN-SOI-FinFET Using Power Gain Parameters
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this work, we have presented, a radio frequency (RF) assessment of nanoscale gallium nitride-silicon-on-insulator fin field-effect transistor (GaN-SOI-FinFET). All the performances of the device have been compared with conventional FinFET (Conv. FinFET) simultaneously. All the results show that the power gains have significantly improved in terms of Gma, Gms, stern stability factor (SS), GMT, and intrinsic delay in comparison to conventional FinFET. Current gain unilateral power gain and have also been evaluated for the extraction of fT (cut-off frequency) and fMAX respectively. fT and fMAX enhance by 88.8% and 94.6% respectively. This analysis has been done at several THz frequencies. The implementation of GaN in the channel reduces the parasitic capacitance and paves the way for high-performance RF applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Reliable Low Power High Speed 4-Bit Array Multiplier using High Performance 1-Bit Full Adders
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Arithmetic operations of binary numbers are the key requirements for all the latest data driven technological advancements including artificial intelligence and machine learning. The present work focuses on the design and development of reliable, low-power and high speed 4-bit array multiplier using high performance mirror and transmission gate based 1-bit full adders. The performance of the proposed 4-bit array multiplier is extensively analyzed for power and delay characteristics at various operational voltages (0.7V to 1.2V) for different technological nodes ranging from 16nm to 130nm.The proposed 16nm technological node 4-bit array multiplier using transmission gate based full-adder circuit dissipates a nominal power of 5.05 µW at an operational voltage of 0.7V, while it dissipates 18.17 µW for mirror full-adder circuit. The power dissipation increases with increasing operational voltage for the proposed 4-bit array multiplier using the two high-performance full adder circuits. The proposed 16nm technological node 4-bit array multiplier yields a delay of 6.37 ps at 1.2V for mirror full adder and the delay increases to nanoseconds regime for the transmission gate based full-adder. The increased delay is might be due to presence of pass-transistors in the transmission gate based full-adder design which require precise transistor scaling at sub-nanometer technological nodes. The simulation analysis suggests the use of mirror full-adder circuit in the development of high speed 4-bit array multipliers; and transmission gate based full-adder circuits for the design of low-power 4-bit array multiplier.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of LG = 16 nm Pulse Triggered Low Power High Speed Data Flip-Flops At Higher Temperatures With a VDD of 0.7 V
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this work, we optimized the Delay & power performance of pulse-triggered (PT) Data (D)-flip-flops (ep-DCO, MHLFF, static CDFF, PFF & CDFF) using SPICE simulations. The flip-flops were optimized for an ultra low V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> of 0.7 V in 16 nm CMOS. The temperature effects on the Data to Q propagation delay & consumption of power of pulse triggered flip-flops have also been investigated by sweeping the temperature from 303K to 383 K with a step increment of 10K. The SPICE simulations results obtained using a V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> of 0.7 V & 16 nm CMOS process points out that PFF with a propagation delay (Data to Q delay) of 11.09 pS (13.22 pS) at 303K (383K) respectively that outperforms other PT-data flip-flops like ep-DCO, MHLFF, static CDFF, & CDFF flip-flops have been considered as key circuits in micro processors, registers & other synchronous VLSI chips.

articleTitle: Effect of Bridging on D-π-D Structures for Efficient Use in Organic Electronic Devices: DFT Investigation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Donor-π-Donor (D-π-D) type structures and the molecular structures based on effective conjugation have interesting optoelectronic properties. These structures are studied for their efficient hole mobility and designing of novel p-type semiconducting materials in the application of organic field effect transistors. These structures are also widely researched for their excellent hole transport properties and their effective use in perovskite solar cells as hole transport materials. Here, two novel molecules have been designed based on D-π-D structure. The effect of bridging units on electronic and optical properties of these compounds have been investigated. The two molecules are S1 (anthracene-thiophene-fluorene) and S2 (anthracene-thiophene-furan-fluorene). They are optimized under the framework of density functional theory (DFT) at B3LYP/cc-pVDZ theory level. In these compounds, anthracene and fluorene act as donors. Thiophene is the bridging molecule in S1, whereas, thiophene and furan are the bridging molecules in S2. The HOMO-LUMO gap energy of S2 is found to be smaller as compared to S1, which may be the result of extended conjugation length in the designed structure. Further, the charge density difference plots have been analyzed using TD-DFT calculations performed at CAM-B3LYP/cc-pVDZ level. The designed novel molecules are expected to be useful for organic optoelectronic applications.

articleTitle: RTL to GDSII Implementation of RADIX-4 Booth Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Booth Multiplier is widely used for high performance signed multiplication by several encoding schemes. Due to the faster generation of partial product, the radix-4 booth Multiplier is very effective, the number of partial products in the multiplier have been reduced to half when compared with conventional multipliers. Carry look-ahead adder is used with the multiplier, which further speeds up the overall process. We have implemented the physical design of a radix 4 multiplier at two different technology nodes i.e. 45nm and 180nm and area, delay, power and bandwidth is calculated using open source tools. In the case of 45nm, chip area of the multiplier was reduced by 95%, power consumption was reduced by 22% and delay by 16.10 %.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Nanocomposite Soft Magnetic Materials: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Conventional micro-sized magnetic materials have same magnetic and electrical properties irrespective of size. The control and tunability of the magnetic properties would be a difficult task. With the development of nano magnetic fillers, various electrical & magnetic properties of magnetic materials are smoothly varied by controlling the size, shape and weight percentage of the nanoparticles. In the recent years many with the addition of nano sized fillers, excellent nanocomposite with unique magnetic properties like high permeability and low coercivity have been developed. The magnetic nanocomposites have shown remarkable improvements in magnetic properties compared to that of conventional counterparts. Henceforth, research investigations in this area is increased. The use of new generation magnetic nanoparticles is demonstrated to be suitable for many power electronics devices such as DC-DC converters, microwave devices, sensors. These magnetic nanoparticles are characterised by moderate magnetic saturation, low coercivity, improved electrical resistivity and low eddy current loss which are also desirable for all the devices.The proposed research presents a comprehensive review of different fillers capable of imparting magnetic properties to the polymer composites. In the proposed research, the advantages of using zinc-cobalt ferrites for the development of magnetic material has been reviewed along with other magnetic fillers such as zirconium, nickel and their combination. The advantages of polymer nanocomposite are improved physio-chemical properties, ease of processing, thermo-mechanical stability, high electric breakdown strength and low cost.The electromagnetic properties can be tailored by incorporating appropriate fillers and weight percentage. Review on assessment of different synthesis and fabrication techniques and the resulting improvement in magnetic properties has been undertaken.

articleTitle: OFF Current Reduction using Zener Tunneling in Tunnel Diode Body Contact Silicon On Insulator
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This paper focus the Zener tunneling behaviour near the drain region of Tunnel diode body contact Silicon On Insulator (TDBCSOI). No such work has been reported to the best of our knowledge. High OFF current and asymmetric structure in TDBCSOI makes it less suitable for binary switching devices. Hence it is essential to have a symmetric structure with low OFF current. In this paper a heavily doped P+ region is embedded below N+ drain region of a TDBCSOI. Analysis of the proposed symmetrical topology exihibits reduction of OFF current by an order of 10.

Author Keywords: Tunnel Diode Body Contact Silicon On Insulator (TDBCSOI)

articleTitle: Analysis of significant parameters of miscellaneuos insulating fluids with Antioxidants
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Transformer have long used mineral oil as an insulant. Mineral oils impact on the environment has been well documented throughout the last century. For such a reason an alternative source of mineral oil is used. Antioxidants are the materials which improve the performance of the vegetable oils in power transformers. Biodegradability, and environmentally friendly in nature are two of the advantages of using vegetable oil. In this work, it is used to select and mix natural fatty acids like sunflower seed oil, Rice bran oil and corn oil in various proportions are used as per the IEC standards. By using IECD standards various critical parameters are determined such as breakdown voltage, Flash point, Fire point and Viscosity.

articleTitle: Effect of Gold thin film deposition in holey-Fiber based liquid sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this article, high sensitivity holey Fiber based Surface Plasmonic Resonance (SPR) liquid sensor is modeled and analyzed. Thin gold metal is deposited to tune the SPR condition in the inner and outer polished surfaces. The circular and elliptical core is used in various sensing techniques such as the Internal and External polished sensing approach for analyzing the performance of this sensor. The full vector finite element method helps the numerical investigation of the sensor in the measurement of the Refractive Index (RI) ranging from (1.33 to1.34). The high sensitivity is obtained (30,000nm/RIU) in the polished external sensing method.

articleTitle: Performance Optimization of Full Swing Adders For Future DSP & Machine Learning Applications Using 16 nm CMOS Process at High Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This article reports the optimization of full-swing (rail-to-rail voltage swing) adders for the efficient realization of booth multipliers that have been considered as the vital blocks for majority of machine learning and DSP (digital-signal-processing) applications. The SPICE simulation results obtained by employing 16 nm CMOS process at 0.7 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DD</inf> indicates that 22-T-HFA with a power & delay of 1.23 µW & 15.84 Ps is best suitable for making high performance booth multipliers compared to 26-T-BFA (Power: 1.36 µW & Delay: 48.9 pS), 28-T-CMOSFA (Power: 0.65 µW & Delay: 42.28 pS), 26-T-HFA (Power: 0.94 µW & Delay: 33.53 pS) and 22-T-TFA (Power: 1.23 µW & Delay: 20.35 pS). Moreover, the thermal drift of speed and power of rail-to-rail voltage swing adders have been systematically investigated by sweeping the temperature from 303K to 383K. High speed rail-to-rail voltage swing adders based booth multipliers have emerged as a key component in the realization of MAC (multiply-accumulate) operations in future CNN computations based hardware platforms.

articleTitle: Effect of thin gold film in Plasmonic based liquid Infiltrates Photonic Crystal Fiber Chemical Sensor:Design and analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Thin gold film-based liquid-filled elliptical core Photonic crystal fiber chemical sensor is modeled and analyzed. Finite element analysis method is used to optimize this design. The Selective metal coating method is applied to enhance the strong photon interaction and efficient Plasmon generation in the metal dielectric interface. The spectral sensitivity and loss peak are obtained in 620nm, 630nm at (1.32 to 1.35) Refractive Index (RI) values respectively. This sensor is applicable in the liquid and chemical sensing areas.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Silicon Nanowire FET for GAA and Pi Gate Configurations
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Short channel effects can affect the performance of a transistor wildly depending on the specifics of the component. This paper investigates and studies the performance of specific silicon nanowire field-effect transistors (SiNW FETs) along varying channel length, temperature, and oxide thickness for two different gate configurations: Gate All Around and Pi gate. The performance will be gauged by the I-V characteristics, mid-channel conduction band profile, and mid-channel charge density profile. The simulation has been carried out by a tool named ‘Multi-gate Nanowire FET’. A Nanowire FET’s drain current decreases by increasing the length of the channel and the thickness of oxide, whereas it rises by increasing the temperature. GAA is also seen to have better device control because of its lower leakage current than any other gate and a higher conduction band energy that is 77.94% (at 15 nm) than the Pi gate.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance of Dynamic Rail to Rail Voltage Comparators Designed Using 16nm Technology with a VDD of 0.7 V
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This article critically studies the role of operating temperature (T) on the speed & power characteristics of dynamic rail to rail voltage comparators implemented using 16 nm CMOS process with an operating voltage of 0.7 V. The thermal investigations have been carried out using SPICE tools. The input stages of the dynamic rail to rail (R to R) fully synthesizable voltage comparators considered in this work were implemented using 3-input NAND gates, 3-input NOR gates and 3-input NAND/NOR gates. The power consumed by the dynamic rail to rail fully synthesizable voltage comparators implemented using 3-input NAND gates, 3-input NOR gates and 3-input NAND/NOR gates are 5.81 µW, 3.6 µW and 8.78 µW respectively. The supreme low power characteristics of dynamic rail to rail fully synthesizable voltage comparators makes them most promising for next generation Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Modeling Nanoscale Depletion Mode MESFET and Comparative Study for Different Semiconductor Materials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the modeling of nanoscale MESFET. The proposed structure uses a Schottky barrier or rectifying contact to reduce fabrication inconvenience by removing the necessity of an oxide layer in a FET. So, it can be an attractive alternative to a typical MOSFET. Modeling the structure in nanoscale ensures minimum transistor size and maximum transistor density in a chip. Ensuring the small dimension of the device, the proposed design has been simulated with COMSOL Multiphysics simulator. The paper also focuses on studying the structure with a variation of materials used as substrate. I-V characteristics like drain current vs. drain to source voltage and drain current vs. gate to source voltage of various materials are investigated. Device performance based on switching ratio is also compared in this study. By using high mobility material, a better switching ratio can be achieved. Due to fast switching, the device can find its usage in high frequency and low power applications.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Effective Hybrid Reversible Multilayer Vedic Multiplier Using QCA-ST
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: "Quantum-Dot Cellular-Automata Spin-Technology" (QCA-ST) based semiconductor devices are the appropriate replacement of "Complementary Metal-Oxide Semiconductor" (CMOS) based digital circuitries at recent digital era due to less complexity, less power requirement and dissipation, higher speed and a possibility to utilize reversible structures easily in 3D multilayer manner. The binary representation of any digital circuit can be presented in this advanced platform using nano-quantum cells. These quantum-cells are used in this work to reconfigure a multi bit Vedic Multiplier design with proper novelty and area-power-delay-complexity optimization. Reversible and majority gates are used in this proposed work in multilayer hybrid manner, which gives a stable result at the time of temperature increment and layer-separation-gap decrement takes place.

articleTitle: Prediction of Electronic parameters of Carbon Nanotube random network Field-effect Transistors under liquid gated conditions using a machine learning approach
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this work, we employed a machine learning approach to predict the performance parameters of CNT bundle network field-effect transistors (FETs). The CNT bundle network FETs are complex system not only due to the random nature of the network but also due to the conductivity and work functions of bundles with both metallic and semiconducting tubes. It is difficult to model a whole network of CNT bundles with unknown conductivity and work function. In a recent work we examined 119 devices for investigate the role of CNT junctions in the electrical conduction and gating of CNT network FETs under liquid gated conditions. In this work we used the experimental data to train and predict the performance using the Support vector machine (SVM) technique. The CNT bundle density of the film measured by atomic force microscope images was used as the input parameter and the on-current, off-current and threshold voltage were the target. We were able to estimate the on current with an accuracy better than 90 percentage. However OFF current and threshold voltage prediction has an accuracy about 82 and 77 percent respectively. The 90-percentage accuracy for the on-current prediction can be attributed to the strong dependency of on-current with the CNT bundle density. However, the off-current and threshold voltage are depending on other parameters namely the presence of metallic CNTs within the bundles and the overall variations in the composition of network. Based on the experimental results, despite the unknown variables, we managed to predict the electronic parameters of a CNT network FETs with using the SVM techniques with significantly high accuracy.

articleTitle: An overview of photovoltaic performance of organic solar cells using PCDTBT:PCBM and PTB7:PCBM active-layer materials
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In recent years organic material based SCs (solar cells) has gained huge attention over traditional photovoltaics due to its low manufacturing cost, renewable feedstock, production scalability, light weight and mechanical flexibility. However the efficiency and durability of organic material based SCs need to be enhanced to make it commercially successful. Active layer material used in organic SC plays a significant role in determining its durability. P3HT:PCBM is the widely used active layer material. Various studies were carried out with different combination of active layer materials to enhance the performance of organic SCs. In this article we have studied the performance of organic SCs fabricated using two different active layer materials namely PCDTBT:PCBM and PTB7: PCBM

articleTitle: Minimizing solar absorption losses in TiO2 particles-based passive daytime radiative cooling coatings
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this work, we have tried to eliminate solar absorption losses in the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> random media in 0.3-0.39 µm wavelength region by introducing a thin layer of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> on top of the coating for passive daytime radiative cooling. We have used Lumerical electromagnetic simulation solver to find out the suitable thickness of the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film. We have shown that for 20 µm and 50 µm thick TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> random media, a TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> thin film of 84 nm and 22 nm thickness is able to reduce the solar absorption losses in 0.3-0.39 µm wavelength region by increasing the reflectivity of the system from 0.08 to 0.52 and 0.7, respectively.

articleTitle: Effect of Single Vacancy Defect on ION/IOFF and Subthreshold Swing in Electrostatically Doped Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Field-effect Transistor with Different Widths
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Graphene has sparked a lot of interest due to its unique physical and electrical properties and emerged as a possible silicon replacement in FET technology. In this paper, the transfer and output characteristics of an electrostatically doped (ED) 7 Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon 10 nm (channel) FET (AGNR- FET) and the transfer characteristics of different (3m & 3m+1 where m is a positive integer) AGNR-FETs (10 nm channel) with three gates are investigated. The atomic interaction between carbon atoms is described by the tight-binding model with the nearest-neighbor approximation. The Poisson and Schrodinger equations are self-consistently solved within the non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF) formalism to simulate the characteristics of the transistors. Results show that a single vacancy (SV) defect at the center of the channel region significantly increases the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio and decreases the subthreshold swing for both 3m & (3m+1) AGNR-FET. For every value of m, the (3m+1) AGNR-FET provides a higher I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</inf> ratio and lower subthreshold swing than 3m AGNR-FET for both cases with or without defect.

articleTitle: RTL & Physical Design Flow of Power Efficient Components of All Digital Phase Locked Loop (ADPLL)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this paper, the physical design (PD) of components of an all-digital based low power phase-locked loop is proposed. Open-source EDA tools are used to convert a RTL design into Graphic Design System (GDSII). Tools includes like Yosys, Graywolf, OpenTimer, Qrouter, and Magic are used for the PD flow for 180nm based and 45nm based technology files in this design. An analysis of the area, power, and delay is done for the 180nm and 45nm technology files based design using EDA tools. The observed area, power, delay, and maximum operating frequency for 180nm and 45nm are 4898.80we,142.65 µW, 1180 ps, 1028.93 MHz and 160.60 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>,7.66 µW, 2118 ps, 1031.54 MHz, respectively. Also, 96.72% area improvement is observed for 45nm technology compared to 180nm technology.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis on H2 plasma assisted growth of graphitic leaves on carbon nanotube
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Numerical conceptual design explaining the growth of graphitic leaves over carbon nanotube (CNT) in Hydrogen (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) plasma environment employing Plasma Enhanced Chemical Vapor Deposition (PECVD) technique is evolved. Growth of linear defect density (investigated via energy balance equation over CNT), CNT, graphitic leaves is explored by varying input plasma power (600-1200W). The results indicate drop in defect density, growth rate of CNT and graphitic leaves with rising plasma power. Obtained theoretical outcomes conform to the experimental studies.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of FinFET based Ternary Inverter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Complex problems have arisen like leakage power and hot electrons causing several drawbacks to the system which tend to affect the efficiency of the system as a whole and the major factor for this problem is the complexity in scaling of the basic transistors. This issue can be prevented or tackled with the implementation of multi-gate transistors. The increase in the number of transistors also tends to increase the circuit complexity of any VLSI chip design thus resulting in the degradation of performance and efficiency of any Binary System. Multi valued logic is seen as the future technology to overcome this issue. The main objective of this work is to analyze performance of FinFET based ternary inverter using T-Spice Simulations.

articleTitle: Predicting the tensile strength of materials applying machine learning for polymeric manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: This study compares and evaluates three Machine learning Algorithm in the field of polymeric film manufacturing. Compression moulding and extrusion-blow moulding were considered under the film manufacturing techniques. In this article, we are investigating how Principal Component Analysis (PCA) may be used to minimize the complexity of predictive and classification models such as k-nearest neighbors, artificial neural networks, and random forests. Using PCA, the provided dataset with 8 input parameters for Experiment 1 and 6 input parameters for Experiment 2 would be reduced and applied Machine learning algorithms for predicting the tensile strength of the material. The k-nearest neighbours (kNN) algorithm showed higher predictive abilities, with a coefficient of determination and Root mean square error of 96 percent and 1.09, respectively, for extrusion-blow moulded films. For compression molding, the ANN achieved 91 percent coefficient of determination and 1.11 as root mean square error. These algorithms can predict or categorize quality indices of commodities generated in multi-parameter manufacturing processes, such as the polymer manufacturing processes under study.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Study on Palladium-ZincOxide System
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The Zinc-Oxide unit’s properties will be investigated in combination with studies of Pd-ZnO Crystal lattice. The semi-conductor then will be emulated with software, and subsequent computations also will be performed to learn more about the lattice’s different states and band structure. The computations are carried out at room temperature. The simulation is run on free open-source application Quantum Espresso, written in FORTRAN C. The main goal of this project is to simulate a Pd-ZnO Unit and compare the results to that of ZnO.

articleTitle: Curing Free, Silver Nano Ink Based Inkjet Printed Fabrics for Bio-Medical Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Inkjet printing plays a vital role in the fabrication of medical cloths that are worn by the patients comfortably. For the acquisition of bio-signals out of the body and to extract the parameters such as temperature, pressure, ECG signals etc conductive electrodes or sensors are used. Hence, conductive patterns or layers are needed to be placed over the body for effective acquisition of bio-signals. Recent wearable medical devices have these sensors as conductive patterns which are integrated with the textile or dress material that the patient wear. There are several methods available for the fabrication of such e-textile materials. One such method is the inkjet printing that overcomes the drawbacks of other traditional methods like dip coating, screen printing, knitting and weaving. In this work, we have fabricated an e-textile cloth by means of inkjet printing using nano silver ink and have proven the conductivity of the printed fabric by means of simple circuitry. This work also shows the comparison of fabrication methods of conductive fabrics and the materials used for the fabrication process.

articleTitle: Investigation of Efficiency Enhancement in Tunnel Junction GaN Light Emitting Diodes
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Without light we can’t imagine this world. In lightning system, LED plays a vital role. In 1950’s, LED by using Gallium Arsenide, was invented. But its output power radiance is too low. To overcome this drawback, Gallium Nitride is used in LED to enhance its glow. After Gallium Arsenide, p++-GaN/i-InGaN/n++-GaN layers are used in Tunnel Junction Structures. These Tunnel Junction Layer (TJL) GaN LEDs were simulated and it is found that output power improved by 36% with respect to that of conventional LEDs. The tunnel junction layers used in such a way to decrease the tunnel junction resistance is called hybrid tunnel junction layers. The resistances of tunnel junction layers were found to be 9.25×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> Ω cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Due to this, there is a drop in its efficiency. To enhance its tunnelling effect, the AlGaN/InGaN is interfaced with it. Thus, the proposed GaN light blooming along with TJL proves it unswerving.

Author Keywords: EBL (Electron Blocking Layer) and WPE (Wall-Plug Efficiency)

articleTitle: CNTFET: Comparative Study of Planar and Coaxial
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: We compare two different orientations of CNTFET in the present paper in order to assess their performance, which are planar and coaxial. Studies and investigation have been done by simulating other performance parameters like IV characteristics, density of state (DOS) vs. energy, potential vs. distance, transmission coefficient vs. energy, and density vs. distance. From the obtained results, it can be analyzed that both of the orientations perform differently at various parameters. For the same chirality and tube length (L = 5 nm and 20 nm), the max drain current for planner orientation is equal to 6 µA, and for coaxial, it is around 18 µA. In the density vs. distance plot for different chirality, the maximum density of charge carriers in coaxial is about 550 M/m at the center of the channel. For a planner, it is around 200 M/m. It is also observed that for planner CNTFET when the dielectric constant (k) increases from 16 to 80, there is a drastic change in current from around 7 µA to 25 µA, but for coaxial, it remains almost constant, which is 15 µA. So, from all this comparison, it was observed that coaxial outperformed planner CNTFET.

articleTitle: Synbiotic hydrogels encapsulating iron and probiotic provide iron bioavailability equivalent to commercially available iron supplements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is a serious concern from which approximately one-third of the global population is affected. Pregnant women and children aged below five years at more risk for the occurrence of IDA. Oral supplementation is the most preferred method to replenish body iron stores. However, the non-compliance of currently available iron supplements generates the need for alternate iron supplements that are more acceptable. The efficacy of currently available oral iron supplements is low because of the multiple side effects that occur due to lower absorption of the major supplemented fraction. This unabsorbed fraction of iron is the major reason behind gastrointestinal discomfort and associated inflammation. This supports the requirement of an alternate iron supplement that enhances the bioavailability with a lower iron dose. Here we have prepared the synbiotic hydrogel co-encapsulating iron and probiotic for improved iron bioavailability. We compared the bioavailability of iron from these hydrogels with commercially available supplements of iron. Iron bioavailability from these supplements was assessed on Caco2 cell line and ferritin levels were measured as a marker for iron absorption. The bioavailability of iron from hydrogels was almost equivalent to commercial iron supplements. This study shows the potential of these symbiotic hydrogels in improving iron status. More insights can be gained on randomized controlled studies on human subjects.

articleTitle: Design and Control Over Morphology of Pseudopeptidic Bottlebrush Polymer/Liquid Crystal Composites
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Polymer liquid crystal composites (PLCCs) with controlled microstructures have several applications in nanotechnology and biology. We, herein, present the design, fabrication, and morphology of pseudopeptidic bottlebrush polymer and nematic liquid crystal composites. An array of extendable submicron to micron size architectures, viz., porous networks, spheres, particles, aggregates, and vesicles is generated from PLCC by appropriately modulating the concentration of polymer, liquid crystal (LC), and solvent in the composite. In addition, the formation of vesicular architectures is monitored with the variation of LC and polymer concentration. The average vesicles size grows from ~250 nm to ~1 µm as the LC concentration increases. The effective loading of LC in the vesicle core is further validated by Raman mapping. Various ultramicroscopic methods such as polarizing optical microscopy (POM), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and atomic force microscopy (AFM) are used to characterize the different microstructures. The methodology presented here, opens up a myriad of possibilities for fabricating high-performance PLCC-based technical devices.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Ge-doped CH3NH3GexPb(1-x) I3 Perovskite Solar Cell By SCAPS-1D Software
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)

A comparative study is done to investigate perovskite solar cell (PSC) performance under AM 1.5G illumination. The structure of solar cells consists of Fluorine tin oxide (FTO) / Tin oxide (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) / (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GexPb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1-x)</inf> I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) / Cuprous oxide (Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O) / metal contact. Thickness, donor concentration, and defect density of the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>GexPb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(1-x)</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> absorber layer are varied on the solar cell characteristics parameters (Fill factor (FF), Power conversion efficiency (PCE), Current density (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</inf>), Open circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</inf>)) of the solar cell device. Apart from that, the effect of anode metal work function is also investigated in this paper. We have optimized our device at 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> of defect density, 1000 nm of absorber thickness, and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> of donor density. The simulation results show that CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.875</inf>Pb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.125</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> based optimized PSC achieved the highest efficiency of 29.20 %. In the last, anode metal contact with a work function greater than 5.0 eV is required to achieve higher efficiency.

articleTitle: A Fresnel-reflection based fiber-optic sensor to study the low-temperature thermodynamics in fluidic mixtures
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: Understanding the behaviour of electrolytic solutions at sub-zero temperatures reveals certain exotic processes. Fluid inclusions which reveal dissolution of two phases, that is ice and salt-hydrates, can only be interpreted in ternary water-salt system. We have developed a fiber-optic sensor based on Fresnel reflection phenomenon to study the phase changes in the mixture of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O-NaCl-CaCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ternary system by cooling them using liquid nitrogen. This fluidic mixture exhibited the separation of antarcticite phase of CaCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>.6H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O at the eutectic temperature of about -51 °C and remained as an unfrozen metastable brine at -200 °C for few minutes before it consolidated into a dense solid. The sensor proved efficient in measuring accurate response which correspond to thermodynamic models in literature and the sensor offers multipoint measurements from remote locations.

articleTitle: Transfer of 2D Nanostructures with Reduced Residues: Influence of Water-soluble Layer and Fabrication of Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The application of 2D materials in electronics and optoelectronics requires a clean transfer process. Although the conventional transfer method has been employed to transfer 2D materials, it is ineffective for device application and large-area transfers. Here, we developed a water-soluble layer-based transfer (WSLT) technology that allows for the damage-free and clean transfer of 2D materials. The transferred film preserves the optical and electrical quality of the as-grown film as a consequence of the clean transfer. In addition, we fabricated a photodetector on MoS2 that has been transferred WSLT process and studied the photoresponse behavior. Our transfer approach significantly improved the photoresponse properties of the photodetector. The photo-to-dark current, responsivity, and detectivity were found to be 65, 0.84 mA/W, and 2.45 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> Jones, respectively. The proposed process can be used to fabricate 2D/3D and 2D/2D heterostructures, flexible devices, etc. Other 2D materials, such as WS2, WSe2, ReS2, and others, can also be transferred using this approach.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Estimation of Bragg Fibers having Double Defect Layers
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The sensitivity of two Bragg fibers having symmetric and asymmetric double defect layers are studied, optimized, and compared. The thicknesses of symmetric defects are 267.24 nm and asymmetric defects are 113.30 nm and 267.24 nm. Two sharp defect modes arise due to the resonance of core and defect modes. The sensitivity of proposed waveguides depends on the separation between defect layers. Right defect mode of symmetric defected Bragg fiber shows maximum sensitivity.

articleTitle: Simulation and Comparison of AlGaN LEDs with Boron Doped GaN Well Using Assorted Aluminium Concentration
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The influence of aluminium concentration on the optical devices of Gallium Nitride Light Emitting Diodes is examined to improve the optical performance of the Light Emitting Diodes. The investigations are done using physical simulator, Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD). Boron doped Gallium Nitride Light Emitting Diodes with four quantum Wells are considered. Radiative recombination, Auger recombination and Polarization models are utilized in simulations. The influence of the assorted aluminum concentration (0.2 and 0.3) in AlGaN/GaN and AlGaN/BGaN Light Emitting Diodes optical performance is presented. The boron concentration of proposed LED is considered as 10%. The analysis on device temperature, radiative recombination rate, luminous power and wavelength with respect to power spectral density are performed to obtain the efficient Light Emitting Diode. The TCAD simulation observations represents that the luminous power and radiative rate of Gallium Nitride Light Emitting Diodes with aluminium mole fraction of 0.2 shows better improvement when compared to 0.3 mole fraction of aluminium.

articleTitle: A Study on CuPc:C60 and other emerging organic materials in solar cell applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The increasing demand for low-cost energy without environmental impact and green-house effect is one of the major driving force in the fabrication of organic solar cells (OSC). Even though OSCs are flexible power sources with light weight, its efficiency need to be improved for large scale commercialization. In recent years various new approaches has been developed to increase OSCs performance parameters. Many new organic materials has emerged as an alternative to widely used P3HT:PCBM organic material. Significant improvement in efficiency was reported with these different active layer materials. In this paper, we have studied the performance of different OSC with CuPc/C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf> blend active material as well as the influence of other emerging organic materials.

articleTitle: Surface damping of plasmon oscillations of a spherical metal nanoshell
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: In this work the surface damping constant of the metal shell nanostructure is calculated on the basis of a model describing the transformation of the energy of the oscillatory motion of electrons into the energy of their thermal disordered motion upon collisions with the shell boundaries. Analytical expressions are obtained that describe the dependence of the damping constant on the parameters of the shell. According to the considered model, the surface damping constant depends non-monotonically on the thickness of the metal shell and makes the largest contribution to the width of the resonance line at values of the shell thickness of the order of several nanometers, turning to zero as the thickness tends to zero. This dependence is consistent with the known results of numerical simulations based on the density functional theory.

publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)

articleTitle: Effect of Co-pollutants on the Photocatalytic Activity of Fe doped ZnO Nanoparticles on the Degradation of Methylene Blue
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: ZnO nanoparticles and Fe doped ZnO nanoparticles with varying Fe concentrations as 0.025, 0.05, 0.075, and 0.1% respective to Zn, was successfully synthesized by the sol-gel method. Synthesized nanoparticles were characterized by X-ray diffractometry (XRD) and Raman spectroscopy. As revealed by both studies Fe has successfully doped to ZnO without causing any lattice distortions. Synthesized catalysts were photocatalytically active in degrading methylene blue under sunlight. The effect of co-pollutants; Rhodamine B, Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, ${\text{P}}{{\text{O}}_4}^{3 - }$ and ${{\text{S}}_2}{{\text{O}}_3}^{2 - }$ on the rate of photodegradation was studied and it was found that Rhodamine B, Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, and ${\text{P}}{{\text{O}}_4}^{3 - }$ reduce the rate and ${{\text{S}}_2}{{\text{O}}_3}^{2 - }$ increases the rate of photodegradation.

articleTitle: Design of Infrared Audio Transmitter and Receiver for point to point data transmission
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Nanoelectronics, Nanophotonics, Nanomaterials, Nanobioscience & Nanotechnology (5NANO)
abstract: The main idea behind this paper is to generate musical notes by infrared radiations. The infrared radiations are transmitted and received by IRLEDs and phototransistor respectively. This paper emphasizes the way by which music is generated and driven by IR rays. Using the circuit one can play songs from his/her iPod, mobile or computer to an external speaker without having to connect them directly through an AUX cable. The circuit comes with many limitations and there are better ways like Bluetooth to play songs wirelessly. The melody produced is heard through the receiver’s loudspeaker. For maximum sound transmission the IRLEDs should be oriented towards IR phototransistor. It can be used in wireless music systems, mobile gadgets and CCTV cameras. Infrared communication is the main mode of short distance communication and has been widely used for point-to-point data transmission.
